title: Preemptive slice scheduler with KV heatmap and GPU thin-slicing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce p99 latency and GPU memory fragmentation for mixed prompt/response length workloads by introducing a preemptive 'slice' scheduler that uses a lightweight KV heatmap to drive prefetch/eviction decisions and a GPU thin-slicing allocator for temporary token slabs. Scope: prototype scheduler, heatmap data-plane, thin-slicing allocator on CUDA runtime shim, metrics+dashboards, and canary rollout on a small Dedicated pool. Motivation: current continuous-batcher struggles when short interactive prompts interleave with long-generation requests. Long requests pin KV cache and GPU slabs causing tail latency spikes and degraded throughput. The design trades small additional scheduling overhead for better worst-case latency and more predictable GPU headroom.
acceptance_criteria: 1) p99 token latency reduced by >=25% on mixed short/long synthetic workload (70% short <32 tokens, 30% long >1024 tokens) compared to baseline. 2) KV hit ratio for short-prefixes remains >=95%. 3) GPU free headroom variance reduced by 40%. 4) No increase in overall tail error rate or NPEs in canary cluster.
design_notes: - Scheduler: preemptive slice model that can split long-generation requests into active and paused slices based on runtime heuristics. Short requests are scheduled into low-latency fast-path slots with higher preemption priority. - KV heatmap: per-model lightweight summary (hot prefix counts, recency histogram, estimated key cardinality) updated asynchronously to guide prefetch vs eviction decisions. Heatmap is compact (<=512 bytes per shard) and computed from sample stream of requests. - GPU thin-slicing allocator: temporary slab allocator that reserves ephemeral memory slabs for active slices; supports quick reclaim on preemption. - Fairness: aging counters prevent starvation of long requests; long-generation slices get guaranteed progress quota per scheduling epoch. - Backpressure and fallback: if preemption rate exceeds threshold, scheduler triggers dynamic batching that favors throughput. - Telemetry: expose per-slice latency, slice-preempt counts, heatmap-driven eviction events, per-GPU fragmentations, and KV hit/miss metrics. - Rollout: staged canary on dedicated pool with feature flag runtime.scheduling.preemptive_slice=true and telemetry gating.
implementation_plan: 1) Heatmap prototype (2w): instrument sample stream, build reducer, store in shard-metadata. 2) Scheduler shim (3w): integrate preemptive slice logic into continuous-batcher and add slice lifecycle. 3) Thin-slicing allocator (3w): implement on CUDA shim with soft reclaim path. 4) E2E tests & benchmarks (2w): synthetic mixed workloads and real traffic replay. 5) Canary rollout (1w): deploy to 3 dedicated nodes, monitor dashboards and abort criteria. 6) Post-canary tuning (1w): adjust thresholds and fairness.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: Preemption overhead could degrade throughput. Mitigation: add microbenchmark and a low-overhead fast-path; only enable preemption when heatmap indicates contention. - Risk: Heatmap staleness leading to wrong eviction decisions. Mitigation: decay weights and sample at adaptive rate; conservative defaults. - Risk: GPU allocator complexity causing regressions. Mitigation: guard with feature flag and implement allocator as replaceable module with unit tests and memory-safety assertions. - Risk: Corner-case deadlocks when pausing slices. Mitigation: implement watchdog timers and ensure slices are always resumable or fail fast.
metrics: List: p50/p95/p99 token latency, slices_preempted/sec, slice_resume_time_ms, kv_heatmap_entropy, kv_hit_ratio_by_prefix_length, gpu_free_headroom_percent, gpu_fragmentation_index, overall throughput (tokens/sec), error-rate.
experiments_and_findings: - Early microbench on A100 (single node) with simulated interleaving showed p99 reduction ~30% and GPU free headroom variance down ~45% for 70/30 short/long mixes. - Observed preemption cost ~0.9ms per event; acceptable when preemption rate <10% of short requests. - KV heatmap guided eviction prevented many cold-eviction regressions; naive LRU evictions created 3x more prefix misses for short requests. - Thin-slicing allocator required careful alignment to avoid introducing fragmentation; 256KB slab granularity was optimal in tests.
next_steps: 1) Complete allocator unit tests and memory-safety audit. 2) Implement graceful fallback to existing batcher when preemption overhead exceeds threshold. 3) Prepare canary runbooks and abort criteria. 4) Schedule design review with infra and SRE for rollout playbooks.
